Chem. 281, 28185–28192 31. Chrencik, J. E., Broun, A., Recht, M. I., Kraus, M. L., Koolpe, M., Kolatkar, A. R., Bruce, R. H., Martiny-Baron, G., Widmer, H., Pasquale, E. B., and Kuhn, P. (2006) Structure 14, 321–330

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Isothermal Titra: EphB2 was dialyzed into 50 mM Hepes, pH 7.2 (at 25 °C), 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM CaCl2, prior to use in calorimetry experiments. The SNEW peptide and all mutant peptides were dissolved in the dialysis buffer. All ITC experiments were performed with a Microcal MCS ITC at 25 °C. ITC experiments were performed as described previously (30, 31).
original_paragraph.Results - Thermodynamic Characterization: Isothermal titration calorimetry studies determined a Kd value of 6 μM for the interaction of the SNEW peptide with human EphB2, which is consistent with the IC50 of ~15 μM previously reported in enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays using mouse EphB2 (supplemental data Fig. S1) (31). In addition, a ΔH of −9.8 kcal/mol was determined. For comparison, binding of the TNYL-RAW peptide to the EphB2 receptor was also tested and found to be undetectable. This is consistent with previous reports that the SNEW and TNYL-RAW peptides are highly specific for the EphB2 and EphB4 receptors, respectively.
original_paragraph.Table 2 caption: Peptides with a Kd noted as >50 μM had binding isotherms that could not be fit because there was no indication of saturation of the binding sites at a peptide concentration of 75 μM.
original_paragraph.Table 2: TABLE 2 Thermodynamic characterization of the EphB2-SNEW interaction Name Sequence Kd ΔG ΔH TΔS μM kcal mol−1 kcal mol−1 kcal mol−1 SNEW SNEWIQPRLPQH 6 −7.1 ± 0.1 −9.8 ± 0.3 −2.6 ± 0.3 SNEW_1 SNQWIPRPLPQH >50 SNEW_2 SNEWISPRLPQH 11 −6.8 ± 0.1 −9.9 ± 0.6 −3.1 ± 0.6 SNEW_3 SNEWILPRLPQH 3 −7.5 ± 0.1 −13.9 ± 0.2 −6.3 ± 0.2 SNEW_4 SNEWIQPKLPQH 6 −7.1 ± 0.1 −11.7 ± 0.1 −4.6 ± 0.1 SNEW_5 SNEWIQPALPQH >50 SNEW_6 SNEWIQPLPQH >50 SNEW_7 SNQWISPRLPQH >50 SNEW_8 SNQWISPRLPQH >50 SNEW_9 SNQWIGPALPQH >50 TNYL-RAW TNYLFSPNGPIARAW >50 a Reported Kd is an average of 2 measurements.
original_paragraph.Discussion: The highest affinity peptide was SNEW_3, containing a single Glu6 → Leu mutation, which resulted in a Kd of 3 μM, or a 2-fold increase in the binding affinity from the original peptide. Mutation of the same position to serine decreased the affinity to 11 μM. Interestingly, the Glu3 to Gln mutation led to a dramatically decreased affinity. It was expected that the polar environment generated by this substitution would assist in stabilization with main chain atoms of residues in the K β-strand of the receptor. Instead, this perturbation adversely affected the existing hydrogen bonding network. This indicates the interaction between Glu3 of the peptide and Val164 of the receptor is more important than expected.

assay_conditions.buffer_composition: 50 mM Hepes, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM CaCl2
